problem: Zero-shot object goal navigation (e.g., ESC, CoW) often fails because the open-vocabulary detector produces false positives (detecting objects that are not there) or misses visible goals, and prior systems are rarely deployed on real robots that lack perfect pose.
motivation: Semantic understanding is the foundation of ZS-OGN exploration and stopping decisions, so detection errors directly lower success rate. The authors want a training-free way to make detection more reliable, and to show the pipeline works in the real world with noisy localization and safety needs.
key_idea: Add a 'Doubly Right' validator: GLIP proposes detections and InstructBLIP cross-checks them against the task instruction, triggering re-assessment on disagreement, on top of an ESC-style frontier exploration pipeline.
insight: Adding a second VLM to verify the first one's detections gives small but consistent gains over ESC (RoboTHOR SR 34.5 to 35.2, SPL 18.2 to 18.3), with larger gains over CoW-OWL on PASTURE. The gains are small on RoboTHOR, so verification helps mostly by filtering errors rather than changing exploration. The paper has no ablation of the validator itself, so the source of the gain is not isolated.
method: Initiator VLM: GLIP detects target objects and room types in the RGB image from prompts P_o, following ESC.
Validator VLM: InstructBLIP receives the image, GLIP detections and a validation prompt P_v, and either advises reassessment (loop back to GLIP) or confirms, setting Goal=True.
Semantic and frontier map: a 2D navigation map built from depth and pose, enriched with GLIP semantics; frontiers are candidate boundaries between free and unknown space.
Commonsense policy: the ESC LLM-based commonsense module (object-room correlations) selects the next frontier; a Fast Marching Method computes the path.

Safe medial-axis path planner (real world): a Nav2 global planner plugin that follows the medial axis of the traversable cost map (via OpenCV thinning), with linear entry/exit segments, plus a DWB local planner for obstacle avoidance.
Real-world localization: RTAB-Map with LiDAR ICP odometry and RGB-D loop closure gives 3DoF pose instead of assuming perfect pose.

setting.backbone: GLIP + InstructBLIP (frozen) with ESC commonsense LLM module
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + pose (real robot: LiDAR + RGBD + IMU via RTAB-Map)
setting.action_space: discrete move forward / turn left / turn right / stop in simulation; waypoint path following (Nav2 DWB) on the real robot
setting.privileged: none (simulation assumes pose is available, as in prior work)

numbers.extra: validation episodes over 15 environments and 12 object categories; ESC baseline reproduced by the authors

numbers_note: Real-world experiments are qualitative only (two apartment trials: TV remote and trash can), with no numbers.
results: On RoboTHOR the method reaches SR 35.2 / SPL 18.3, slightly above reproduced ESC (34.5 / 18.2) and well above CoW CLIP-OWL (21.9 / 13.4). On PASTURE it gets average SR 23.0 / SPL 13.7 versus OWL 21.1 / 12.6. Real-world tests on a Unitree B1 quadruped in an apartment found the TV remote and trash can.
limitations: Gains over ESC are marginal and there is no ablation or statistical analysis of the validator, and no analysis of its added compute or latency.
Real-world evaluation is only two qualitative trials with no success-rate statistics, and the system can make poor early choices in featureless areas (a bare room mistaken for a bathroom).
The validator's prompts and its reassessment loop are underspecified, with no stopping criterion or retry limit described.
